speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry with regard to the Report of the Auditor-General, wherein it stated that test checks found that JTC premises may have been sublet to about 26,000 business entities without JTC's approval (a) whether JTC has completed investigations into all identified business entities and confirmed cases; and (b) what are the penalties imposed on affected tenants, lessees and sub-lessees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: There are another 12,400 related entities of JTC lessees and tenants.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For these 12,400 related entities, even if there was subletting of space, there would not have been any potential loss of revenue as the subletting fees would not have applied.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Based on preliminary investigations, JTC has found that a significant number of them are using JTC premises as their registered address even though they are not physically operating out of the premises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Again, since they are not operating out of these premises, these cases do not involve any unauthorised subletting of space.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: JTC is strengthening its processes as well as its inspection regime and it will make use of data analytics to better detect and reduce future incidences of unauthorised subletting.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: It will take enforcement action against lessees or tenants for confirmed cases of unauthorised subletting.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I have two follow-up questions, the first of which is in relation to the 400 cases thus far identified.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In terms of these cases, what would the penalties be and what would have been the loss in the sublet fees that JTC would have collected.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The second supplementary question is in terms of the sharpening of the analysis to improve the inspection regime, specifically with the use of data analytics which the Second Minister has affirmed.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: What has really changed between now and then?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Since the implementation of this change, has there been more cases of unauthorised subletting that have been discovered and how would the Ministry assure the efficacy and efficiency of such a new regime?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As to the extent of the sublet fees and the unauthorised part, it is still a subject of further investigations.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will take all active steps and measures to recover these fees that are owing and, in cases where clear-cut illicit subletting has been proven, we will not hesitate to take legal action to enforce it.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On the part about using data analytics, indeed, in terms of the understanding of the ability to register a business address using a premise, this is one of the policies which we need to tighten and realign.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But, of course, these are on a regular time basis to inspect the premises whether there is illegal subletting.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Now, over and above what we had done in 2019, on top of the regular inspections, we are also going into random spot checks as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, the intensity of the checks, audits and inspections has also increased significantly.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At this particular point in time, I am not at liberty to share what is the frequency of these checks and inspections.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But suffice to say that this is at a much more focused pace and, obviously, we are going to put a lot more effort and work into tightening it.
